key: The movement of the Tao By contraries proceeds; And weakness marks the course Of Tao’s mighty deeds.
s: Opening a chapter on where all things come from, the verse tells how the Tao moves and works; Wang Bi, on chapter 40, reads the movement as reversal, the high founded on the low, the noble on the humble, and non-being the use of being.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 40, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 道德經 (王弼本), the 華亭張氏 edition, revision 2354026
opened.locator: chapter 40, comment on 反者道之動

evidence.words: 高以下為基，貴以賤為本，有以無為用，此其反也。
evidence.gloss: The high takes the low as its foundation, the noble takes the humble as its root, being takes non-being as its use: this is its reversal.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Problem holds: “being working through non-being” reads as a progressive verb. Recast as “non-being the use of being”, which is 有以無為用 (being takes non-being as its use), and “the noble rooted in” shortened to “the noble on” to parallel “the high founded on”; opening shortened to “Opening a chapter on where all things come from” as the critic proposed.
